subject: Private endpoint outbound policy — NAT vs HTTP proxy + DNS / IP allowlist checklist
body:
--- Message 1 ---
From: Daniel Liu <daniel.liu@finteq.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on outbound restrictions for Redwood private endpoint

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the walkthrough today. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we prepare the network design:

1) We need a firm list of outbound IPs that the private endpoint might reach for control-plane callbacks and telemetry. Can you confirm whether Redwood publishes a stable egress IP set for private deployments, or whether we should expect dynamic ranges?
2) Regarding egress controls: do you recommend a NAT gateway with static SNAT IPs, an HTTP(s) forward proxy, or a combination? We have strict host-level allowlisting on our perimeter, so minimizing the list of IPs is important.
3) Any guidance on DNS resolution — should we allow outbound DNS to internet resolvers or force conditional forwarding to our internal DNS?

We tried to capture the ask in the attached spreadsheet. Can you route this to your network/security folks? Looking to finalize by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior Platform Engineering, Finteq

--- Message 2 ---
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Liu <daniel.liu@finteq.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on outbound restrictions for Redwood private endpoint

Hi Daniel —

Thanks, and great questions. Looping in Hannah (product security) and Vivek / David (network) to give concrete guidance. High-level answers below — we will follow up with a short matrix and config snippets: see attachments.

- Egress IPs: For hosted control-plane callbacks (only when using Redwood Private with hybrid control plane), we provide a small, documented set of stable egress IPs per region. For fully air-gapped "on-prem" installs there are no Redwood-published IPs; control-plane is customer-hosted. We will include the region-specific IP set in the matrix.
- NAT vs proxy: We typically recommend a dual option depending on customer posture:
  * If you need minimal operational complexity and can accept a handful of SNAT IPs, use a managed NAT (static elastic IPs) and allow TCP/443 to our published egress list. This is ideal for TLS-only outbound to our control endpoints and model artifact pulls.
  * If your security team requires application-layer inspection or domain-level allowlisting (FQDNs), use an HTTP(s) forward proxy with explicit CONNECT/TLS passthrough rules. This lets you enforce ACLs and monitor outbound domains.
  * For maximum control, we support placing a proxy in front of the private runtime to enforce per-route allowlists, plus NAT for non-HTTP traffic.
- DNS: We recommend conditional forwarding. The runtime performs service discovery for a short list of Redwood domains; forward queries for those domains to your upstream resolvers that can apply DNS filtering. We discourage allowing unrestricted public DNS from the runtime.

I will attach a short "egress decision matrix" and a couple of proxy snippets that map to our runtime ports. Hannah, Vivek, can you add anything critical?

Best,
Aisha
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 ---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Daniel Liu <daniel.liu@finteq.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on outbound restrictions for Redwood private endpoint

Thanks for the ping — adding network specifics so Finteq's ops team can map to their stack.

Key constraints and recommendations (practical checklist):

1) Ports & protocols:
   - TLS (TCP/443) outbound to redwood-control.redwood.ai and model-cdn.* (must be allowed).
   - gRPC (if using streaming integrations) over TLS on TCP/443 as well.
   - NTP (UDP/123) optional if you don't have an internal time source — prefer internal NTP.
   - DNS (UDP/53/TCP if fallback) — conditional forwarding strongly preferred.

2) IP allowlisting vs FQDN:
   - We publish per-region egress IPs for the hybrid control-plane and artifact access. Add those IPs to your perimeter ACLs.
   - Our artifact CDN uses third-party cloud CDN IPs (changeable); use FQDN allowlist for CDNs if you cannot tolerate frequent IP churn.

3) NAT guidance:
   - Use a small set of static SNAT IPs behind your NAT gateway; tag them and document rotation windows.
   - If using cloud NAT, reserve EIPs and advertise them to security.

4) Proxy guidance:
   - Proxy should allow CONNECT to our root domains and block all other external SNI unless explicitly required.
   - If you require TLS interception for threat inspection, be aware this will break certificate pinning used by parts of our runtime; use proxy allowlist for those endpoints instead.

5) Logging / Audit evidence:
   - Export proxy allow/deny logs and NAT flow logs for 90 days to satisfy most SOC2 evidence requests.

Attachments: small matrix and proxy snippets attached.

Vivek
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

--- Message 4 ---
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 12:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on outbound restrictions for Redwood private endpoint

Hi all — quick security notes to ensure Finteq's compliance team is comfortable: 

- We provide a signed, versioned IP list and canonical FQDN list for use in allowlists; include a pull-hash in your procurement docs so you can show the exact snapshot used during testing.
- Our runtime can operate with TLS-only egress; we do not require TLS interception. If your org requires interception, please schedule a short test with us — some clients opt to carve a small CA-exempt exception for our endpoints.
- For SOC2 audit evidence, provide the reviewer the NAT IPs + proxy logs + our published hash for the egress list. We will sign an attestation letter for integration dates.

Thanks,
Hannah
Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Liu <daniel.liu@finteq.com>

Appreciate the clear guidance — that helps a lot. Next steps on our side:

- We will provision two static EIPs for the runtime NAT and add them to our perimeter ACL for TLS outbound next week.
- We prefer proxy-by-exception: allow CONNECT to your canonical FQDNs, block interception for those endpoints, and keep full interception for everything else.
- Can you confirm the signed IP/FQDN list location and the cadence for updates? Also please share the small attestation letter Hannah mentioned.

I'll attach our internal network plan after provision. Thanks again — cc'ing our infra-security distribution for audit visibility.

Regards,
Daniel
Finteq Platform Team
